prize_parts.citation: for discoveries of the physiology and active forms of glucagon-like peptide-1 that enabled incretin-based treatment of type 2 diabetes and obesity

statement.case_for: The round-1 exchange did not move me off B033 and it sharpened why. Every member reached the same configuration independently, and each tied it to the science: incretin physiology and proglucagon processing, the biologically active GLP-1(7-36) peptide, receptor biology with the therapeutic rationale, and long-acting agonists confirmed in large independent trials for glycaemia, weight and cardiovascular and renal outcomes. The mechanism is stable, the discovery can be stated in one sentence, and maturity is not in question. Holst and Drucker are secure under any resolution of the priority record, so most of the prize does not depend on the disputed point. I support a single-part prize as the working configuration.
statement.case_against: The third name is still the exposed point. Mojsov's priority for the active truncated peptide is contested, Habener and other early proglucagon investigators are not on our credit list, and Knudsen, whose team made liraglutide and semaglutide, falls outside the three-person cap. A discovery-only prize can be read as honouring the mechanism and not the medicine. I still cannot audit the priority history from the supplied material, and a prize that rests on an unverified third name carries a real fairness risk that the unanimity of our first-round positions does not remove.

responses.point: She would keep Knudsen in mind as the strongest replacement if Mojsov's priority cannot be defended, and would rather use a separate part or a different year than drop Holst or Drucker.
responses.response: I agree with the structure of that argument. Holst and Drucker are fixed, so the only open slot is the third, and the real test is whether Mojsov's identification of the active GLP-1(7-36) form is secure. From the supplied material I have no basis to displace her, and replacing her with Knudsen would turn a discovery citation into a development citation without a stated principle. If the evidence on the active peptide were shown to fail, I would move to Knudsen in that slot and not to a two-name prize. I also take your point that a separate part for development is more honest than a quiet swap, but I do not see a development part that this year's shortlist supports.

responses.point: She argues that an unresolved third name is a reason to scrutinise the allocation, not a reason to prefer a cleaner but lower-impact candidate, and that the citation should make the therapeutic consequence visible.
responses.response: I agree on both points. Choosing a candidate with a tidier trio only because the GLP-1 credit is awkward would trade scientific weight for neatness, and I will not do that. On the citation, my wording already says the discoveries enabled incretin-based treatment of type 2 diabetes and obesity, which carries the therapeutic arc without crediting the developer. I also accept your correction on Rosenberg: the cleaner CAR-T configuration is June and Sadelain, and I note you agree Eshhar's absence is the larger problem, which keeps B039 as an alternative and not my preferred part.

responses.point: He says the prize is for a discovery and that the translation step depended on established physiology, so the discovery trio can carry the therapeutic arc through the wording, and he now sees Hall and Schreiber as the cleaner TOR core.
responses.response: I agree that the translation was possible because the physiology was already established, and that is the principle I am applying to the Knudsen question. I would add that the principle has a cost I want recorded: Knudsen's long-acting analogues are what made the drugs, so the committee should state openly that she is left out by the cap and by the discovery emphasis, not because her work is lesser. On TOR, I welcome your movement to Hall and Schreiber. It matches my view, and it does not change my ranking, because the clinical impact outside transplantation and a few cancers remains much narrower than the biology.

responses.point: He would have the committee test a Holst and Drucker pair before deciding on Mojsov, and he favours a trio for CAR-T by keeping Rosenberg.
responses.response: A Holst and Drucker pair is a fair test and I think we should run it. It would be a defensible fallback, but it would leave out the identification of the active peptide, which is the step that connected proglucagon biology to a therapeutic hormone, so I judge it the weaker configuration unless the priority evidence goes against Mojsov. On Rosenberg, I still disagree with you. His adoptive cell transfer and early gene-engineered T-cell trials are real precedent, but they are not the CAR construct, and a trio would credit the field rather than the engineered receptor. I would not make this decisive since B039 is not my preferred part.

responses.point: The chair ranks BCR-ABL lower because the upstream Philadelphia chromosome and BCR-ABL discoveries are not covered by the credited names, and he flags that early chimeric receptor pioneers matter more than the Rosenberg question.
responses.response: The upstream point is correct and it limits B009 as a standalone prize. I keep it as my second alternative because the clinical result, a durable remission from a targeted inhibitor, is among the clearest in oncology, but I accept it would look incomplete without the upstream names. I agree with you that B039 and B009 share a structural problem, in that the credited names do not cover the full discovery chain, and this is another reason I support B033 alone as the working configuration.

uncertainties: Whether Mojsov's priority for the active GLP-1(7-36) peptide is secure enough for the third slot, which I cannot verify from the supplied material and for which I am relying on recollection.
Whether Habener and other early proglucagon investigators, who are not on the credit list, should change the allocation among Drucker, Holst and Mojsov.
Whether the committee will say openly that Knudsen is excluded by the discovery emphasis and the cap, and not by the merit of her work.
Whether the absence of Eshhar from the credited names should stop B039 from ever being a fair configuration as listed.
statement.conflict_note: No change from round 1. No specific conflict is apparent from my profile for B033, B039 or B009. My documented spatial transcriptomics and single-cell work is not among the shortlisted achievements. My co-authorship with Rickard Sandberg and with others named in the profile does not involve any credited shortlisted name. I infer no ties from shared institutions or topics.
